newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-NZ CRUSH AUSTRALIA TO CLAIM WORLD SUPREMACY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NZ CRUSH AUSTRALIA TO CLAIM WORLD SUPREMACY.

text.p: The All Blacks confirmed they were the benchmarks for world rugby on Saturday with a rampaging 30-13 victory over the Wallabies in a test match at Christchurch.
Australia, fresh from a 2-0 series win over five-nations champions France, had no answer to New Zealand's powerful scrum, superior handling skills and ferocious attack.
"Australia was beaten by a better team," Wallaby coach Greg Smith said after the match.
"The All Blacks are the best team in the world."

The test began with great intensity from both sides and only penalties were traded inside the first 20 minutes. But Australia soon began to buckle under the sustained pressure applied by the All Black scrum, which set up a platform for the New Zealand loose forwards to run amok.
All Black flanker Josh Kronfeld scored the game's first try after wing Jeff Wilson burst down the sideline, outpacing his opposite Joe Roff to set up the opportunity.
New Zealand could not be denied another try in the 30th minute when their scrum pushed the Australians back over their goal-line for number eight Zinzan Brooke to fall on the ball.

Then, two minutes from halftime, Kronfeld again linked onto the end of a rampaging passage of play to cross for his second try. The Wallabies hardly touched the ball in the first half and went to the break trailing 23-3.
Australia began the second spell with renewed vigour and determination, but couldn't capitalise on their chances in the face of a rock-solid All Black defence.
The Wallabies suffered a crushing blow when mid-way through the second half centre Pat Howard fell badly in a heavy tackle and was stretchered off the field with an ankle injury.
That allowed the All Blacks to once again take the upper hand and they remained camped out on the Wallaby goal-line until Zinzan Brooke, in his 50th test, drove over for his second try.
Australia finally touched down for the first time with 10 minutes remaining on the clock. Flyhalf Tim Horan threw a dummy pass to waltz across the line -- but the death knell had already sounded.
"The All Black scrum was very good and we found it hard to cope with, all game," Smith said. "An even bigger worry was our inability to hold onto the ball."
All Black coach John Hart paid tribute to his tight five, who relentlessly shoved their opposition backwards throughout the match.
"We scrummed outstandingly well for 80 minutes," Hart said.
"We knew we had to get the scrum right. It was a crucial win for us."

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham, 14-Ben Tune, 13-Daniel Herbert, 12-Pat Howard (17-James Holbeck, 54th minute), 11-Joe Roff, 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan, 8-Troy Coker, 7-David Wilson, 6-Brett Robinson, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Matt Cockbain, 3-Ewen McKenzie, 2-Marco Caputo, 1-Richard Harry.

New Zealand - 15-Christian Cullen, 14-Jeff Wilson, 13-Frank Bunce, 12-Lee Stensness, 11-Tana Umaga, 10-Carlos Spencer, 9- Justin Marshall, 8-Zinzan Brooke, 7-Josh Kronfeld, 6-Taine Randell, 5-Ian Jones, 4-Robin Brooke, 3-Olo Brown, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), 1-Craig Dowd.
